name: hotspot
purpose: Marks a real control as a step of a tutorial. It wraps the control and, while a tutorial that names its `hotspotId` runs, draws a small marker beside it. The current step's marker pulses and opens the step in a popover: the step's title, `Step n of N` with the task's name, the instructions, and Previous / Next (Finish on the last step). Outside a running tutorial, or outside a `TutorialPanel.Provider`, it renders only the wrapped control, so hotspots can stay on a page for good.
useWhen: A tutorial step is about one control on the page, and the reader should see where it is.
The page runs inside a `TutorialPanel.Provider` and offers guided tutorials from its help region.
avoidWhen: A permanent tip on a control → use `hint` or `popover`.
A new feature announcement with no tutorial behind it → use `popover` or an `alert`.
Help text for a form field → use the field's `helper-text`.
related: tutorial-panel` — the provider holds the steps a hotspot shows; the panel lists and runs the tutorials.
popover` — the overlay the current step opens in.
help-panel` — static help without a guided run.
bestPractices: Wrap exactly the control the step is about; keep the marker beside it, not inside a long row.
Use `side="start"` when the control sits at the end of a row and the marker would overflow.
One `hotspotId` per control and per page. The same id on two elements opens two popovers.
Keep step content short: the popover is a small surface over the real UI.

props.name: hotspotId
props.doc: Matches the `hotspotId` of a tutorial step; the marker shows while that step's tutorial runs.

props.name: side
props.doc: Which side of the wrapped control the marker sits on, in reading direction.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The real control the step is about.
